sections.title: The letter gé
paragraphs: The letter name is (gé) /ʒe/. Its main sound is heard in (gare) /ɡaʁ/, which means train station. This letter has two different spoken sounds in French. It can also be completely silent at the end of some words.

sections.title: Making the sounds
paragraphs: For the first sound, press the back of your tongue against the soft roof. Release the trapped air and make your throat vibrate. Put a hand on your throat to feel the buzz. For the second sound, push your lips forward into a loose ring. Raise the front of your tongue toward the upper gums. Push the air through with your voice on.

sections.title: Reading the letter
paragraphs: You hear the first sound before the vowels a, o, u or before a consonant, like in (gros) /ɡʁo/. You hear the second sound before the letters e, i, or y, as in (gel) /ʒɛl/ and (girafe) /ʒi.ʁaf/. At the end of some words, the letter is not pronounced at all, as in (doigt) /dwa/ and (sang) /sɑ̃/.

sections.title: Common mistakes
paragraphs: Do not add a d sound before the second sound, like in the English word judge. It must flow smoothly like the middle sound of the English word vision. Keep your tongue slightly further forward and let the air glide out without an explosive burst.
